relations.subject: Charles Rockwell Lanman
relations.evidence: Lanman graduated from Yale College (Phi Beta Kappa) in 1871

relations.subject: Charles Rockwell Lanman
relations.evidence: and was a graduate student there (1871–1873) studying Greek under James Hadley and Sanskrit under WD Whitney. He then eventually earned his doctorate degree at Yale in 1873.

relations.subject: Charles Rockwell Lanman
relations.evidence: He also studied Sanskrit under Weber and Roth and philology under Georg Curtius and August Leskien in Germany (1873–1876).

relations.subject: Charles Rockwell Lanman
relations.evidence: Lanman was appointed a professor at Johns Hopkins University when it opened in 1876. He was a professor of Sanskrit at Hopkins from 1876 to 1880.

relations.subject: Charles Rockwell Lanman
relations.evidence: In 1880, Lanman moved to Harvard University where he was the first to preside over the department of Indo-Iranian Languages... He was also the inaugural holder of the title of Wales Professor of Sanskrit.

relations.subject: T. S. Eliot
relations.evidence: During 1911 and 1912 one of his students at the Harvard Graduate School was T. S. Eliot, who was undertaking a doctorate in philosophy.
